name: Weglot
tagline: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Weglot, translate a small static site build and generate localized routes at deploy time. The hard boundary is website proxy, automatic discovery, machine translation, seo routing, and hosted delivery, plus translation memory, collaboration, and deployment integrations.

prompt:
Build an advanced website translation and localization pipeline to serve as a personal substitute for Weglot.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and integrations with translation APIs (like DeepL or Google Translate).
The core loop is: automatically detect content on a static site, route it through translation APIs, generate localized routes at deploy time, and provide a visual management dashboard.
1. Content Detection: Build a script that scans HTML files and extracts all text nodes, images with alt text, and SEO metadata.
2. Translation Management System (TMS): Create a local dashboard (Next.js) to manage projects, locales, keys, and translations. Include a "Visual Editor" mode that overlays an iframe of the site and allows clicking elements to edit their translations in-context.
3. SEO Localization: Automatically generate 'hreflang' tags and localized URL slugs. Ensure all SEO metadata is translated and injected properly.
4. AI Translation & Glossaries: Use machine translation for a first pass. Implement a custom glossary feature to force specific translations for brand names or technical terms. Allow users to review and approve translations before publishing.
5. Import/Export: Support standard localization file formats: JSON, YAML, PO, and XLIFF, strictly preserving placeholders and pluralization forms.
6. CI/CD Integration: Provide token-authenticated pull and push endpoints to integrate with GitHub Actions or other CI pipelines, ensuring translations are synced during the build process.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command. Store all user data locally by default. Put secrets in .env. Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states. Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs. Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path. Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps. Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts. Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
